title: Introduce graceful schema coercion shim for tool-calls and streaming
author: Aisha Rao
description: Context: Customer integrators and existing SDKs observed intermittent client-side failures when the server upgraded the request/response schema for structured outputs and tool/function calling. Failures were most prominent during streaming sessions where field reorderings or deprecated keys caused the OpenAI-compatibility layer to emit malformed events. Motivation: avoid hard-breaking schema flips by adding a server-side, opt-in coercion/shim layer that (1) accepts older request shapes and coerces them into current runtime schema, (2) emits deprecation warnings to telemetry and response headers, and (3) stabilizes streaming chunks by normalizing event envelopes across schema versions. This PR implements an experimental shim plus opt-in headers to allow gradual rollout and developer testing. It is intentionally conservative: coercions are only applied when the request includes an opt-in header and when an explicit compatibility rule exists. Checklist: - [x] implement request coercion rules (old->new) for tool/function call payloads - [x] stabilize streaming event envelopes by normalizing "id"/"event_type"/"payload" semantics across v1/v2 - [x] add X-Redwood-Schema-Prefer and Prefer-Schema-Version headers for opt-in/telemetry - [x] emit deprecation telemetry events with Linear keys - [x] add comprehensive unit + integration tests (streaming harness) - [x] document behavior in compat guide (internal) Non-goals: do not auto-coerce unknown/ambiguous shapes; do not change default server behavior for requests without opt-in header. Links: design: https://linear.redwood.com/ENG-2094 design notes; incident: SUP-887 (incidents related to streaming tool-call failures).

description_short: Add an opt-in server-side schema coercion shim to make schema upgrades non-breaking for streaming and tool/function calls; adds headers, telemetry, tests, and docs.
release_notes: Add experimental 'Prefer-Schema-Version' and 'X-Redwood-Schema-Opt-In' headers for opt-in schema coercion.
Server can accept legacy tool-call/request shapes when opt-in header is present; will emit deprecation telemetry.
Stabilizes streaming event envelopes across schema versions when shim is enabled.
notes_for_ops: Feature is behind opt-in header. Operations: watch telemetry key 'schema.coercion.applied' and 'schema.coercion.errors'; rollout can be toggled by enabling header rewrite in edge proxy. Default behavior unchanged for traffic without header.
risk_assessment: Low-medium: changes are opt-in and guarded by explicit headers. Risk comes from incorrect coercions; mitigation: limited rule registry, comprehensive test harness, and telemetry to detect mismatches.
how_to_validate: 1) curl with Prefer-Schema-Version: v1 and sample legacy tool payload -> ensure response uses new schema; 2) run streaming harness w/ header and verify event envelope shape; 3) confirm telemetry events 'schema.deprecation.warn' and 'schema.coercion.applied' emitted; 4) run regression suite (tests/compat & tests/streaming).
follow_up_work: Expose rule registry for customer opt-outs (ENG-2101)
Add auto-suggest rules in Redwood Console for common client SDKs
Operationalize gradual rollout via edge header rewrites and canarying
